Metric steps

The steps behind the metric definitions in inst/workflow/2_metrics/. Input_HysLaw, Input_QtProlongation and Input_SafetyAE feed the three participant-level flagging metrics; Input_Deaths, Input_Participants and Input_ParticipantDays feed the descriptive census metrics, which publish a number, carry no threshold, and call Flag_None where a flagging metric calls gsm.core::Flag().

Input_HysLaw()
Participant-level Hy's Law candidate tier from liver chemistry
Input_QtProlongation()
Participant-level QTc prolongation tier from ECG data
Input_SafetyAE()
Participant-level serious / related / discontinuation AE tier
Input_Deaths()
Study-level count of participants who died
Input_Participants()
Study-level count of the participants a domain names
Input_ParticipantDays()
Study-level total of participant-days
Flag_None()
Publish a metric's rows without a flag

Study census

The safety overview’s denominators. Being rebuilt on the metric steps above (obot.roadmap#274); this function is unchanged until step four.

SafetyCensus()
Study census, exposure and follow-up for a safety overview

Reports

The steps behind the report definitions in inst/workflow/4_modules/. SaveWidgetReport writes a widget module; the Report_Census* helpers and Report_SafetyCensus assemble and render the safety census, reading the figures the census metrics published and computing nothing of their own (obot.roadmap#274).

SaveWidgetReport()
Save a safety widget as a standalone HTML report
Report_CensusFigures()
The census figures, as the report presents them
Report_CensusCoverage()
The data-coverage rows, as the report presents them
Report_CensusProvenance()
What each census metric published, verbatim
Report_SafetyCensus()
Render the census report
